title: Trapped by Your WORDs: (Ab)using Processor Exception for Generic Binary Instrumentation on Bare-metal Embedded Devices
problem: Embedded platforms lack comprehensive binary manipulation tools for dynamic analysis and security evaluation of closed-source drivers and libraries. Existing instrumentation approaches depend on OS features or have corner cases that prevent application to bare-metal firmware environments.
motivation: Security analysis of embedded drivers and libraries is critical for embedded system supply chain security and vulnerability detection in closed-source components.
method: The technique harnesses processor exceptions—events triggered when the CPU encounters special conditions like invalid instructions or memory protection violations—to intercept code execution. When an exception occurs, the instrumentation code's exception handler activates, observes what's happening, then lets the original code continue. This works on bare-metal devices with no operating system, and correctly handles edge cases like nested exceptions that break existing tools.
key_novelty: This work shows that processor exceptions—events the CPU triggers when encountering special conditions—can be the foundation for monitoring binary code on bare-metal systems without an operating system.
contributions: First generic binary instrumentation framework for bare-metal embedded devices using processor exceptions
Eliminates OS dependency constraints that limit existing dynamic analysis tools
Enables runtime analysis and security assessment of closed-source embedded firmware
primary_theme: Exception-based binary instrumentation for bare-metal embedded security analysis
